limitations: NCff mice carry Nestin-CreERT2 and two floxed Bax alleles on a mixed C57BL/6-129/SvEv background. The primary contrast is tamoxifen versus vehicle within NCff, starting at at least eight weeks. Reporter NCY versus NCffY comparisons use separate littermate groups both receiving tamoxifen; Cre-negative Bax-floxed controls are another comparison.

The manipulation reduces Bax-dependent cell death in the Nestin stem/progenitor lineage; it is not a selective increase in birth rate or a dentate-newborn-neuron-only intervention. Olfactory-bulb survival also changes. Reporter recombination is a proxy, and altered cell properties or other lineage effects remain alternative mediators.

Behavioral testing is generally at 14-18 weeks with both sexes, but fear conditioning, discrimination, extinction and clearance use males. Experiments and analyses were blinded to genotype or treatment. A complete randomized allocation, exclusion, cage and prospective sample-size manifest is not reported.

Weak-tetanus LTP is a population field response, not a birthdated single-cell recording. Eight-week assays without bicuculline use eight slices/six vehicle mice and eleven slices/seven tamoxifen mice; with bicuculline they use four slices/three vehicle and six slices/three tamoxifen mice. Slice-level statistics do not reconstruct animal-level independence.

Main experimental text and Methods, all four main figures, and the text of all 28 supplement pages were read. Supplementary pages 5, 16-19, 24 and 26-27 were visually inspected. Raw recordings, animal-level behavioral data and executable analysis code were not obtained or replayed.

studies.finding: The Bax manipulation increases surviving cell labels and selected LTP and behavioral responses. It supports task-specific intervention effects, while unique mediation by neuron number and irradiation-based cognitive necessity remain unresolved.
limitations: NCff mice carry Nestin-CreERT2 and two floxed Bax alleles on a mixed C57BL/6-129/SvEv background. The primary contrast is tamoxifen versus vehicle within NCff, starting at at least eight weeks. Reporter NCY versus NCffY comparisons use separate littermate groups both receiving tamoxifen; Cre-negative Bax-floxed controls are another comparison.

The manipulation reduces Bax-dependent cell death in the Nestin stem/progenitor lineage; it is not a selective increase in birth rate or a dentate-newborn-neuron-only intervention. Olfactory-bulb survival also changes. Reporter recombination is a proxy, and altered cell properties or other lineage effects remain alternative mediators.

Behavioral testing is generally at 14-18 weeks with both sexes, but fear conditioning, discrimination, extinction and clearance use males. Experiments and analyses were blinded to genotype or treatment. A complete randomized allocation, exclusion, cage and prospective sample-size manifest is not reported.

The eight-week dentate BrdU assay labels on days 9-18 and counts on day 56; only a subset is NeuN-positive. Counts, marker fractions, proliferation and mature output are distinct. The olfactory and running BrdU schedules differ. Reporter neuron counts per section are not whole-dentate totals.

Weak-tetanus LTP is a population field response, not a birthdated single-cell recording. Eight-week assays without bicuculline use eight slices/six vehicle mice and eleven slices/seven tamoxifen mice; with bicuculline they use four slices/three vehicle and six slices/three tamoxifen mice. Slice-level statistics do not reconstruct animal-level independence.

Main Figure 2c alternates the order of contexts across days, whereas the discrimination Methods describe training context A followed one hour later by similar context B. The exact per-animal schedule requires reconciliation. The nine-day ratio analysis reports treatment P=0.023; its day F/degree-of-freedom/P combination also needs correction. Handling of a zero sum of freezing scores is unspecified.

Contextual freezing discrimination is a behavioral proxy for pattern separation, not a direct measurement of DG neural population codes or general memory improvement. Supplementary protocol variants have treatment P=0.38 and P=0.06 despite interactions or day-specific differences; they cannot be pooled as uniformly positive main effects.

Irradiation uses separate ten-week-old Bax-floxed mice and three 5 Gy exposures on days 1, 4 and 8, with behavior four months later. Regional irradiation is not a selective newborn-neuron ablation or a rescue experiment. Recall samples are eight sham/nine irradiated mice, versus seven/nine in discrimination; the missing sham inclusion is unresolved.

Supplementary Figure 14 reports an overall discrimination-ratio treatment P=0.1 and interaction P=0.3. Late within-group differences are not a between-group necessity test. Its day-five F(1,14)=4.34/P=0.04 pair needs reconciliation; no replacement biological P value is calculated here.

Running is a shared-cage exposure: two wheels for four to five mice, beginning five weeks after treatment. Figure 4 shows behavior on days 64-84. Individual running dose and cage independence are unresolved. Increased locomotion complicates an isolated anxiety interpretation, and home-cage activity has a separate sample.

Reported null outcomes are assay- and cohort-specific, not equivalence tests. Supplementary Figure 18 contains invalid negative F notation and conflicting novelty-suppressed-feeding significance; Figure 19 has a control-label conflict. Figure 20 contains a malformed marker percentage. These values are not silently corrected or admitted as quantitative defaults.

Granule-layer volume Methods and caption disagree on group size. Sholl analysis selects complex neurons and traces collapsed z-stacks; its null is not a unique three-dimensional geometry. Axon-length and cell-count cohorts cannot establish packing density or a complete output route without matched measurements.

Main experimental text and Methods, all four main figures, and the text of all 28 supplement pages were read. Supplementary pages 5, 16-19, 24 and 26-27 were visually inspected. Raw recordings, animal-level behavioral data and executable analysis code were not obtained or replayed.

Null object-recognition, water-maze, avoidance, extinction and clearance endpoints do not mean that every measured behavior is unchanged: the novel-object habituation locomotor interaction is significant. Multiple cohorts and distinct pre- and post-training manipulation schedules must remain separate.

studies.finding: Peripheral challenges evoked neural readouts, while selected neural manipulations changed circulating cytokines. Activation improved high-dose endotoxin survival but increased bacterial tissue load in a different live-infection protocol. A complete descending immune circuit is not identified.
limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Fos-based TRAP2 labeling is followed by at least four weeks before functional rechallenge to restore LPS sensitivity. LPS-TRAPed, Dbh-cre, Vglut2-cre and Vgat-cre populations are not identical. Dbh expression does not measure norepinephrine release or identify a unique molecular mediator.

For standard cytokine chemogenetics, Methods specify CNO at 2 mg/kg twelve hours and 1 mg/kg one hour before challenge; schematics and captions show only the one-hour pretreatment. mCherry controls receive CNO. Saline/LPS tests use the same cohort at least seven days apart, whereas hM3Dq/hM4Di versus mCherry comparisons use separate groups. Blood ELISA at two hours does not identify cytokine-producing cells.

Cre-defined nodose activation perturbs marker-defined neurons; it is not selective activation of the TRPA1 channel or CALCA peptide. TRPA1 neurons include different stimulus-responsive subgroups. Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. In vivo responses do not establish direct cytokine binding to a neuronal receptor; epithelial or immune intermediates remain possible. Referenced imaging procedures have not been fully audited.

Survival experiments use separate Trpa1-cre nodose and Dbh-cre cNST cohorts after high-dose LPS, with repeated 5 mg/kg CNO dosing. Figure 6 shows survival through nine days, not a lifelong or clinical outcome. Separate infection experiments use oral Salmonella and eight CNO injections beginning twelve hours before inoculation; bacterial load is measured in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes at day five.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence or proof of no pathway contribution. The corticosterone null is a two-hour circulating concentration, not complete exclusion of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal mediation. Extended Data 3 reuses the Figure 2c saline/LPS data; it is not an independent replication.

The cNST transcriptomic atlas pools tissue from five animals; 4,008 cells and expression clusters are not independent animal replicates, anatomical coordinates or a measured connectome. Rabies labeling supports an anatomical input interpretation, not synaptic efficacy. Main text calls the rabies reporter dsRed while Methods and Extended Data 12 specify GFP; panel 12d depicts Trpa1 but repeats Calca in its quantitative caption. No tracing fraction is calibrated.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

The DSS Methods specify CNO in the experimental cohort drinking solution, while Figure 6 says all animals received CNO. Matched control exposure and intake need resolution before a selective DSS mechanism is admitted. This issue does not change the separately described injected-CNO LPS or infection protocols.

studies.correctionCheck: Publisher and PubMed metadata and exact-DOI correction searches checked. DOI 10.1038/nn.4542 is a commentary, not an erratum. No identified correction resolves the listed reporting conflicts; this is not exhaustive notice surveillance.
studies.finding: Capillary potassium evokes upstream dilation and hyperpolarization and increased RBC passage under specified conditions. Endothelial Kcnj2 deletion reduces the whisker perfusion response without eliminating it.
limitations: Adult male mice; Online Methods state two to three months, but Supplementary Table 2 reports mean ages of 14.8 weeks for C57BL/6 and 17.0 weeks for knockout laser-Doppler cohorts. No exact universal age range is admitted. No randomization, blinding, prospective sample-size calculation or exclusions were reported.

Kcnj2 deletion uses constitutive Tek-Cre, not adult-induced capillary-only deletion. Isolated cEC currents and control smooth-muscle currents support endothelial attribution but do not exclude developmental effects or establish restriction to one vascular segment. Identical listed genotyping primer pairs require verification before protocol reproduction.

Whole-cell currents are measured with 60 mM external potassium; this recording solution is distinct from 10 mM focal capillary stimulation, 15 mM cortical superfusion and physiological neural release. Kir2.1/Kcnj2 is the primary molecular identity. Ba2+ also blocks vascular Kir channels outside capillary endothelium.

CaPA is an isolated, pressurized preparation with sealed capillary ends, not normal flowing blood. Diameter, upstream smooth-muscle voltage and in vivo flux come from separate recordings. Membrane-potential recordings use wortmannin to suppress movement. Estimated conduction speed is inferred from distance and onset, not voltage measured along every endothelial cell.

In vivo measurements use acute cranial windows and alpha-chloralose/urethane after isoflurane surgery. RBC flux is cells per second; velocity is distance per time; laser Doppler gives a relative tissue perfusion signal. None is BOLD, oxygen consumption or an exact anatomical network reconstruction.

Peak RBC flux is the maximum one-second bin in an approximately seventeen-second post-stimulus interval relative to about three seconds of baseline. Velocity is sampled in the peak-flux bin, not an independently selected peak. Paired observations and nested capillaries are not independent mice.

The Figure 4 diameter null concerns eighteen capillaries in seven mice; the authors state that sampled measurement sites lacked pericytes. Upstream diameter uses eight paired experiments in seven mice. The local null does not exclude pericyte effects at other segments or prove equivalence.

Whisker responses persist after endothelial Kcnj2 deletion. Surface barium has a broader target range and leaves residual perfusion responses. The potassium source during neural activity and the complete intercellular route remain unresolved; potassium ejection bypasses the physiological release step.

Supplementary Figure 5 reports five preparations but paired t statistics with five degrees of freedom; Figure 7 reports group sizes inconsistent with its unpaired-test degrees of freedom. Supplementary Table 1 and Table 2 also reverse control-line sample counts for the flow comparisons. Exact quantitative calibration requires animal-identified measurements and resolution.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence. The selected SK/IK activation protocols do not exclude every calcium-dependent endothelial channel. The LFP control tests selected spectral bands, not complete neural activity, and the TTX potassium experiment does not identify the physiological potassium-releasing cell.

Raw recordings and custom MATLAB LFP software have not been obtained or reproduced. The reporting checklist and main text do not provide a resolved access route. No numerical edge weights, universal minimal carrier counts or independently validated full pathway are assigned.
